title: As Suno Rolls Out Its New AI Models With Industry Licenses, What Does That Mean For the Music Business?
key_facts: Suno announced its v6 AI music models on Wednesday 9 Sep 2026, saying they are its first made in partnership with the music industry.
Suno retired all its past models; Warner Music Group says the new model is fully licensed.
Deals cited are with Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe (Believe's announced 8 Sep 2026).
Suno avoids the word 'licence' and its product chief says the money paid is not in exchange for training.
Suno is still being sued by Universal Music Group, Sony Music, SOCAN and Koda, and lost a copyright case in Germany brought by GEMA.
Payment is a revenue share to rights holders, who decide how it is paid out; how much reaches artists is unclear.
The American Federation of Musicians is suing Warner over lack of transparency about compensation.
Suno plans later products for remixing and sampling that would need artist opt-in.
quote_evidence: On Wednesday (Sept. 9), Suno announced its new line of AI music models, which the company says are its first "in partnership with the music industry."
But Suno never uses the word "license."
This will be a revenue share.
why_it_matters_hint: A test of whether AI music firms will pay rights holders, but terms are private.
notes: Older news re-dated: the article says the announcement was on Wednesday 9 Sep 2026, a month before the pool date (10 Oct 2026). Score lowered for staleness.
